name: Vung Tau food guide
summary: Eat bánh khọt on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, one small crisp cake at a time, wrapped in herbs and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce. Then sit down to a stingray hotpot, crab bánh canh, or squid hủ tiếu, and end the evening choosing your fish at the Back Beach night market.
body: Bánh khọt is the snack a Vung Tau trip turns on: bite-size cakes fried in small molds, crisp outside and soft inside, with shrimp on top. Wrap each one in lettuce and herbs and dip it, rather than pouring the fish sauce over the stack. It is not a folded bánh xèo.

Lunch and dinner are pots and bowls. Stingray hotpot comes sour-sweet with greens and bún, and crab bánh canh is thick noodles in crab broth with fried shallots and lime. Breakfast is hủ tiếu mực, a pork-bone and dried-squid broth with squid, shrimp, and quail eggs.
After the swim, walk to the Back Beach night market, pick fish, crab, or shellfish, and choose how it is cooked. Snails come by the plate on Lý Tự Trọng, Kha Vạn Cân, and Trương Công Định.
Bánh canh Long Hương is a breakfast bowl at 11 Cách Mạng Tháng Tám in Long Hương, Bà Rịa, not a stall on the peninsula. Nguyễn Trường Tộ and Hoàng Hoa Thám are the streets for bánh khọt.
specialtiesLead: Start with bánh khọt and bánh tiêu, then work through the bowls, the seafood plates, and the sweets.

sections.heading: Seafood bowls and plates
paragraphs: Vung Tau eats from the sea: hotpots for the table, noodle bowls for breakfast, and plates of snails and oysters for the evening.

spots.name: Lau ca duoi
spots.address: Trần Hưng Đạo, Trần Phú, and Hùng Vương
spots.note: A sour-sweet stingray pot for the table, the fish soft and sweet with no small bones. The broth carries bamboo shoots, or tamarind and pineapple, with greens and bún on the side.

spots.name: Banh canh ghe
spots.address: Tú Xương, Võ Thị Sáu, and Lê Lai
spots.note: Thick, chewy noodles in crab broth with sweet crab meat, fried shallots, herbs, and lime. The broth can be creamy with coconut milk or a lighter seafood stock.

spots.name: Bun rieu tom
spots.note: Naturally sweet shrimp stock with tomato, shrimp cakes, tofu, squid, and pork. Greens go in the bowl and shrimp paste stays on the side.

spots.name: Hu tieu muc
spots.note: The breakfast bowl: pork-bone and dried-squid broth with squid, shrimp, fish cake, and quail eggs. Lime, bean sprouts, and herbs come beside it.

spots.name: Goi ca mai
spots.note: Thin raw cá mai in a tangy, sweet, slightly spicy dressing of lime, fish sauce, and garlic. Roll it in rice paper with herbs and peanuts.

spots.name: Chao hau
spots.note: Soft rice porridge with oysters, fried shallots, cilantro, and fish sauce. Order it after a day out.

spots.name: Oc
spots.address: Lý Tự Trọng, Kha Vạn Cân, and Trương Công Định
spots.note: Ốc hương, ốc mỡ, ốc len, and ốc móng tay, fried with tamarind, grilled with scallion oil, roasted in salt, or tossed in butter and garlic. The beach restaurants and the Back Beach night market serve them too.

spots.name: Hau nuong pho mai
spots.address: Beach restaurants and the Back Beach night market
spots.note: Oysters grilled with cheese, a shared plate next to the snails at the evening seafood tables.

spots.name: Banh canh cha ca
spots.address: Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm and Phan Bội Châu
spots.note: Soft noodles and chewy, strongly flavored sea-fish cakes in a clear, naturally sweet bone broth. Eat it for breakfast or a light dinner.

spots.name: Bun sua
spots.address: Cô Giang and Tô Hiến Thành
spots.note: Crisp jellyfish in a light, lightly sweet broth of bones and seafood, with greens, chili, and lime.

spots.name: Goi cuon tom
spots.address: Cô Giang and Xô Viết Nghệ Tĩnh
spots.note: Boiled shrimp, greens, and rice noodles rolled in rice paper, cool and not greasy. Dip it in mắm nêm or peanut sauce.

spots.name: Bun oc
spots.note: Fresh snails and soft noodles in a sour broth of tomato and tamarind, with greens. Stir in mắm tôm and chili to taste.

spots.name: Lau tom 5 ri
spots.note: Small, firm, naturally sweet shrimp in a bone and seafood broth soured lightly with tamarind or pineapple. Greens, mushrooms, and bún or mì go with the pot.

sections.heading: Snacks and sweets
paragraphs: Between meals, Vung Tau snacks on fried dough with mung bean, salted-egg sponge, grilled-beef bánh mì, hot tofu, and cold cups of avocado and durian.

spots.name: Banh bong lan trung muoi
spots.note: Sponge cake with salted egg yolk, cheese, and pork floss. The sweet cake plays against the salty yolk and cheese.

spots.name: Banh mi bo nuong
spots.note: Marinated grilled beef, fragrant, soft, and sweet, in a baguette with herbs, cucumber, and a special sauce.

spots.name: Tau hu nong
spots.address: Thùy Vân and Hoàng Hoa Thám
spots.note: Hot, soft tofu, mildly rich and lightly fragrant, with sweet-sour fish sauce or soy sauce.

spots.name: Kem bo sau rieng
spots.note: A cold cup of fresh avocado and ripe durian, rich, gently sweet, and fragrant with durian.

spots.name: Khoai tay dai
spots.note: Crisp long potato sticks under a rich sauce, usually mayonnaise, cheese, or chili.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: Bánh canh Long Hương is the neighbor’s bowl, from Long Hương in Bà Rịa rather than the peninsula.

spots.name: Banh canh Long Huong
spots.address: 11 Cách Mạng Tháng Tám, Long Hương, Bà Rịa
spots.note: Translucent, chewy-soft noodles in a rich bone broth, usually with fish cake, pork hock, or shrimp and pork. It is a breakfast bowl.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Nguyễn Trường Tộ and Hoàng Hoa Thám are the bánh khọt streets. The Back Beach night market is where you choose the fish and how it is cooked.

spots.name: Nguyen Truong To
spots.address: Nguyễn Trường Tộ, Back Beach side
spots.note: The street for bánh khọt, on the Back Beach side of town. One kitchen at number 14 opens 7:00–14:00 on weekdays and 7:00–20:00 on Sundays.

spots.name: Hoang Hoa Tham
spots.note: The other bánh khọt street, running inland toward the whale hall. Hot tofu is sold here too.

spots.name: Back Beach night seafood market
spots.nameVi: Chợ hải sản đêm Bãi Sau
spots.note: After dark, pick fish, crab, or shellfish and choose how it is cooked.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Start the day with hủ tiếu mực, squid, shrimp, fish cake, and quail eggs in a pork-bone and dried-squid broth. Bánh canh chả cá and bún ốc are the other morning bowls, and bánh canh Long Hương is breakfast in Bà Rịa.

seoTitle: Vung Tau food guide — bánh khọt and the seafood bowls
seoDescription: Bánh khọt on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, stingray hotpot, crab bánh canh, squid hủ tiếu, and your pick of the catch at the Back Beach night market.
